text: 瓢虫：凭什么嫖娼不合法!ji女也是靠自己的劳动赚钱！
en: Piao Chong: On what grounds is patronising prostitutes illegal! Prostitutes also earn money through their own labour!

text: 凭什么看不起人家！
en: On what grounds do you look down on people!

text: ji ：5555既然哥哥们都说我是合法的，相亲的时候一定不会嫌弃我的工作吧。
en: ji: 5555 Since all you big brothers say I am legal, you surely will not look down on my line of work when we go matchmaking.

text: 瓢虫：哪来的野鸡滚一边去。
en: Piao Chong: Where did this streetwalker come from? Piss off.

text: 都搁着揣着明白装啥糊涂呢。
en: You are all just acting the fool while knowing perfectly well what is going on.

text: 说白了，瓢虫就是想没有代价的随便嫖娼，因为合法了才不用提心吊胆的被抓，被罚款进橘子，合法了还有人专门给卖淫女体检让他不怕得病放肆的嫖，可劲的嫖。
en: To put it bluntly, Piao Chong simply wants to patronise prostitutes freely and without cost, because once it is legal he will not have to live in fear of being caught or fined and hauled off to the station; once it is legal there will even be people giving prostitutes special medical check-ups so that he can fuck without fear of disease, whoring to his heart's content.

text: 瓢虫根本不把卖淫女当人，只是当作商品来供自己使用。
en: Piao Chong fundamentally does not treat prostitutes as human beings, but merely as commodities for his own use.

text: 把人商品化，把女人商品化，对瓢虫来说就是：这种好事凭什么不合法！
en: To commodity people, to commodity women — to Piao Chong this means: on what grounds should such a good thing be illegal!

text: 希望瓢虫从自己做起，移民新加坡，干一份合法的卖屁股工作，工作之余再去嫖嫖ji女，钱赚到了，也爽到了，真是神仙生活。
en: I hope Piao Chong will start with himself, emigrate to Singapore, take up a legal arse-selling job, and in his spare time go and patronise a few prostitutes; he will have earned his money and had his fun — a truly blessed life.

text: 快去建设新加坡，应嫖尽嫖。
en: Go and build up Singapore quickly; whore to your heart's content.

text: 非常ridiculous的问题，为什么呢？
en: A most ridiculous question — but why?

text: 倒不是说把这样一个问题放到公共场合讨论有什么不雅，而是因为整个围绕合法性/正当化展开的讨论在我看来都非常无聊。
en: It is not that there is anything indecent about raising such a question for public discussion; rather, the entire discussion revolving around legality/legitimation strikes me as utterly boring.

text: 不过鉴于有观点认为只有文化保守主义的路径才能逻辑一致地为拒绝卖淫合法化辩护（并且相当多的人尤其是自由主义者都是这样样认为的），我不得不给出另一条完全不涉及所谓道德批判或文化保守主义的回应，而这个新路向本身就是以批判整个合法化/正当化的问题建制为前提的。
en: Nevertheless, given that some hold the view that only a cultural-conservative path can defend the rejection of prostitution legalisation in a logically consistent way (and a good many people, especially liberals, think exactly this), I am compelled to offer a different response that does not involve any so-called moral critique or cultural conservatism — and this new direction is itself premised on a critique of the entire problem apparatus of legalisation/legitimation.

text: （这里没有任何贬低的意思，而仅仅是澄清立场，而我拿这个回答做例子，恰恰认为是他把问题说明白了）
en: (There is no intention here to belittle anyone; I merely wish to clarify my position, and the reason I take this answer as an example is precisely that I think he has laid the problem out clearly.)

text: 如何反驳支持卖淫合法的人？
en: How does one refute those who support the legalisation of prostitution?

text: - 飞奔的马达的回答 - 知乎
en: - Answer by Fei Ben De Ma Da - Zhihu

text: 不需要太多精力，我们只要略微打量一下我们周围的现实，就可以发现娼妓业从来没有因为所谓非法化而消失，也不可能因合法化而消除使它产生的社会根源与它所面临的社会歧视。
en: It does not take much effort; we need only glance briefly at the reality around us to find that the prostitution industry has never disappeared because of so-called criminalisation, nor can legalisation eliminate the social roots that give rise to it or the social discrimination it faces.

text: 就此而言，合法化问题无非只是社会物质生活的变迁在法律上层建筑的反映罢了。
en: In this sense, the question of legalisation is nothing more than a reflection in the legal superstructure of changes in society's material life.

text: 娼妓是同整个社会形态联系在一起的，而并非仅仅与法律保持单个的联系。
en: Prostitution is bound up with the entire social formation, and not merely in a single relation to the law.

text: 倒不如说，法律仅仅是整个链条的最后的与最微不足道的环节罢了。
en: One might even say that the law is merely the final and most insignificant link in the whole chain.

text: 一旦我们意识到这一点，这个合法化的问题就应当被转化为如下三个新问题：
en: Once we become aware of this, the question of legalisation ought to be transformed into the following three new questions:

text: 第一，娼妓制度从近乎绝迹到勃然复兴的社会根源是什么？
en: First, what are the social roots behind the prostitution system's sudden revival from near-extinction?

text: 这个问题是本质地同下一个问题联系在一起的：值得思考的并不是性的解放或身体自由，而是为什么性总是要求以合法化的商品形式出场？
en: This question is essentially bound up with the next: what is worth pondering is not sexual liberation or bodily freedom, but rather why sex always demands to appear in the commodified form of something legalised?

text: 两者的断裂是极其清晰的，性解放或性自由在很多国家面临的都已经不再是合法化诉求，而是社会承认（今日赛国似乎在法律上相对保守而现实中相对开放），它的敌人则是文化保守主义或父权制；然而商品形式却是必然地同市场经济与资本主义联系在一起的。
en: The rupture between the two is extremely clear: sexual liberation or sexual freedom in many countries no longer faces a demand for legalisation, but rather a demand for social recognition (today's Sai Guo seems relatively conservative in law yet relatively open in practice); its enemies are cultural conservatism or the patriarchy. And yet the commodity form is necessarily bound up with the market economy and capitalism.

text: 二者的范围和内涵都是截然不同的，而正是由于社会形式的遮蔽，才使得人们将其无意识地重合在一起，并且以为道德批判就是批判的全部。
en: The scope and content of the two are utterly distinct, and it is precisely the obscuring effect of social forms that leads people unconsciously to conflate them, and to suppose that moral critique is the whole of critique.

text: 对这一问题的思考把我们带向了对所谓合法性概念本身的质疑：对于某一特定的社会而言，合法性/正当性又意味着什么？
en: Reflection on this question leads us to call the very concept of legality into question: what does legality/legitimacy mean for any given society?

text: 但是我现在不打算回应这些问题，而是继续把讨论向深入推进。
en: But I do not intend to answer these questions now; rather, I shall continue to push the discussion further.

text: 在贴出的回答里，对于”性商品合法化“的讨论是从如下两个维度切入的：
en: In the answer that was posted, the discussion of "the legalisation of sexual commodities" proceeds along the following two dimensions:

text: 首先，性器官或者性特征是否有与人的其他身体器官或特征在道德上的本质不同，以至于通过性器官或特征赚钱天然就比通过四肢/脑力等其他器官赚钱来的不道德？
en: First, is there an essential moral difference between sexual organs or sexual characteristics and a person's other bodily organs or characteristics, such that earning money through sexual organs or features is inherently more immoral than earning money through other organs such as the limbs or the brain?

text: 其次，在进行经济活动组织的时候，是性器官相关的工作啊不道德/不能合法化是因为它极容易受到黑恶势力的控制？
en: Second, in organising economic activity, is it that work involving sexual organs is immoral/cannot be legalised because it is extremely susceptible to control by vicious criminal forces?

text: 还是它受到黑恶势力的控制恰恰只是因为它长期被看做是不道德/违法的？
en: Or is it that it is controlled by vicious criminal forces precisely because it has long been regarded as immoral/illegal?

text: 我会指出这里至少存在着在我看来非常严重的视野空缺。
en: I would point out that here there exists, in my view, a very serious blind spot in perspective.

text: 这个空缺首先就在于他似乎完全是在一个空空如也的而不是真实运作的社会中来考察性商品合法化问题的。
en: This blind spot lies first of all in the fact that he seems to examine the question of sexual-commodity legalisation entirely within an empty society rather than a real, functioning one.

text: 一方面，他没有讨论性产业是在怎样的社会形态、以怎样的方式开展自身的，另一方面，他也没有深入到自己得以提出“合法化命题”的社会前提中去。
en: On the one hand, he does not discuss the social formation within which, and the manner in which, the sex industry conducts itself; on the other hand, he also fails to probe the social premises that enable him to raise the "legalisation thesis" in the first place.

text: 而这在马克思眼中就是一种深刻的幻想。
en: And in Marx's eyes this is a profound illusion.

text: 娼妓或性商品在古代一直是合法化乃至官方化的，然而这和身体自由或者性解放毫无关联，甚至和我们今天的商品化也没有什么联系，因为它甚至从来都没有摆脱奴隶地位与人身依附关系，而与之相关的人口买卖哪怕民国时期都很难称得上非法。
en: Prostitution or sexual commodities were in antiquity always legalised and even officialised, yet this had nothing to do with bodily freedom or sexual liberation, nor indeed much connection with our commodification today, for it never shook off the condition of slavery and personal dependency; and the associated trade in human beings could hardly be called illegal even during the Republican era.

text: 因此，当他询问“性特征有什么不同以至于靠性赚钱就更不道德时”，他已经是完完全全立足于资本主义社会来进行讨论的了，而资本主义的特定形态由此就构成了伦理学或道德学的不言自明的前提。
en: Thus, when he asks "what is so different about sexual characteristics that earning money through sex is all the more immoral," he is already discussing things entirely from the standpoint of capitalist society, and the specific form of capitalism thereby constitutes the self-evident premise of his ethics or moral philosophy.

text: 也正因此，对于娼妓业的批判应当以批判其得以出场的全部社会历史后台为前提（性产业本身就有自己的不同历史形态），而不是什么单纯的对性/道德的讨论。
en: And precisely for this reason, critique of the prostitution industry ought to be premised on a critique of the entire social-historical backstage that enables its appearance (the sex industry has its own distinct historical forms), rather than being any mere discussion of sex/morality.

text: 举例而言，我们完全没有必要在“性”的层面上批判旧的娼妓业，就像我们也没有必要以“性”之名反对奴隶制一样——尽管的的确确有奴隶主会rape奴隶，无论男女。
en: By way of example, we have absolutely no need to criticise the old prostitution industry at the level of "sex," just as we have no need to oppose slavery in the name of "sex" — even though it is true that slave-owners would rape slaves, male or female.

text: 反之，纯粹关于合法化/正当化的讨论，不管是支持还是反对，也都不过是以不同的方式承认现实的基本建制。
en: Conversely, a purely legalisation/legitimation discussion, whether for or against, is nevertheless nothing more than an acknowledgement of the basic apparatus of reality in different guises.

text: 当马克思在说哲学家以不同的方式解释世界时，他真正想说的其实是这个。
en: When Marx said that philosophers have interpreted the world in different ways, what he truly meant was precisely this.

text: 进一步的，当我们考察性产业的现实运作时，我们也并不需要考察它与黑社会之间的某种联系——尽管这个联系是必然的。
en: Further, when we examine the actual operation of the sex industry, we do not even need to examine its certain connection with organised crime — even though that connection is necessary.

text: 相反，对于支撑着性产业的社会根源进行分析，就足以使我们提出不仅废除性产业而且废除全部现存社会的主张了。
en: On the contrary, an analysis of the social roots that sustain the sex industry is enough to enable us to advance the proposition not only of abolishing the sex industry but of abolishing the whole of existing society.

text: 就其人员组成来看，社会底层占了绝大多数，而其中相当一部分则是下岗职工与无法获得对应生活资料的人。
en: In terms of its personnel, the social underclass makes up the overwhelming majority, and a considerable portion of these are laid-off workers and people unable to obtain the means of subsistence corresponding to their needs.

text: 在这里发挥作用的正是资本主义的相对人口规律和产业后备军机制。
en: What is at work here is precisely capitalism's relative law of population and the mechanism of the industrial reserve army.

text: 因此这本身就是资产阶级统治加强的表现。
en: Thus this is in itself an expression of the strengthening of bourgeois rule.

text: 而在其现实运作层面，绝大多数性商品并不是以个体形式，而是要么依附于夜总会要么依附于平台经济而流入市场，其中的剥削是触目惊心的。
en: And at the level of its actual operation, the overwhelming majority of sexual commodities do not enter the market in individual form, but rather flow in either attached to nightclubs or attached to the platform economy, and the exploitation therein is shocking.

text: 再次，社会的压迫与歧视机制是实打实的，而很多人讨论问题的时候完全把它们当作不存在一样。
en: Once again, the mechanisms of social oppression and discrimination are real and tangible, yet many people discuss the issue as if they simply did not exist.

text: 这里不涉及什么道德判断，而是实实在在的客观描述。
en: This involves no moral judgement whatsoever, but is a down-to-earth, objective description.

text: 而这一机制常常与资本主义合谋：不仅是向资产阶级提供特权与优越感，而且为无产阶级提供意识形态工资，因为他们可以通过歧视他人来暂时摆脱自身的被歧视处境。
en: And this mechanism often colludes with capitalism: not only does it furnish the bourgeoisie with privilege and a sense of superiority, it also provides the proletariat with an "ideological wage," because they can, by discriminating against others, momentarily escape their own discriminated-against condition.

text: 在这里，道德与其说是保守的，倒不如说是为资本主义所需要的。
en: Here, morality is less conservative than it is something capitalism requires.

text: 而自由主义者给出的回应则是可笑的，他们指出其他工作也一样没有尊严、受社会性歧视、被资产阶级嘲弄。
en: The response offered by liberals is laughable: they point out that other jobs are likewise devoid of dignity, subject to social discrimination, and mocked by the bourgeoisie.

text: 这事实上无非是用人的无尊严来为人的无尊严辩护，用统治阶级本身来论证阶级统治的正当性。
en: This is in fact nothing more than using people's lack of dignity to defend people's lack of dignity, and using the ruling class itself to justify the legitimacy of class rule.

text: 仅此三点就决定了，我们并不需要抬高或贬低性，也不需要讨论它是生产性的还是非生产性的，而仅将它视为雇佣劳动的一种，就足够对性的商品化提出指责了。
en: These three points alone determine that we need neither elevate nor denigrate sex, nor discuss whether it is productive or unproductive labour; it suffices to regard it as a kind of wage labour in order to lodge an accusation against the commodification of sex.

text: 在这里，激进的性自由与对于性的商品形式的废除，完全可以无冲突地结合在一起，而并不需要诉诸某种文化保守主义。
en: Here, radical sexual freedom and the abolition of the commodity form of sex can be combined entirely without conflict, and need not appeal to any kind of cultural conservatism.

text: 而且，这里存在着一个极其重要的颠倒：那些看似对性持开放态度的人，与其说是追求性的自由解放，不如说是只有当性表现为商品形式时才允许性以合法化的地位出场。
en: Moreover, there exists here an extremely important inversion: those who appear open-minded towards sex, rather than pursuing the freedom and liberation of sex, might better be described as permitting sex to appear in a legalised status only when it takes the commodity form.

text: 在这里重要的不是性，而是由性取得的剩余价值和商品景观。
en: What matters here is not sex, but the surplus value and the commodity spectacle obtained through sex.

text: 性是美的，而且是可以公开的，但是必须被放到橱窗里。
en: Sex is beautiful, and may be made public, but it must be put in the shop window.

text: 而一旦我们以更加激进的态度提出有关命题，比如说，我支持裸体自由，任何人都有权裸体出现在公共空间，并且只要他们愿意就可以在任何地方开impart（我真心支持，尽管我还没有这样做，但那是社会因素导致的），这些人中又会有几个人支持呢。
en: Yet once we advance the relevant propositions with an even more radical attitude — for instance, I support nudity freedom: anyone has the right to appear naked in public space, and may hold an impart anywhere they please (I genuinely support this, even though I have not done so myself, but that is owing to social factors) — how many of these people would then support it?

text: 尽管那个时候他们给出的反驳将是非常可笑的——因为他们发现自己将不得不成为那个自己口中的文化保守主义者才可能保卫那个可笑的公共空间。
en: Even though the rebuttals they would then offer would be utterly laughable — for they would find that they had to become the very cultural conservative they themselves denounce in order to defend that ridiculous public space.

text: 回过头来看合法性争论，我们也就能发现。
en: Looking back at the legality debate, we can then perceive.

text: 法不过是现实阶级关系的表达（法不需要成为工具，它只需要与社会保持一致就已经是在维护社会形态与阶级利益了，而它和社会是必然保持一致的），因而所谓合法也不过是要求新增的法规/删去某一法规后法的形式系统仍然能保持为一个完善的整体，就像性产业已然经深深扎根于发达资本主义社会的肌体中。
en: Law is nothing more than the expression of real class relations (law need not become a tool; it need only remain consistent with society to already be upholding the social formation and class interests, and it is necessarily consistent with society); thus so-called legality merely demands that, after a new statute is added or some statute deleted, the formal system of law can still be maintained as a complete whole — just as the sex industry has already taken deep root in the flesh of advanced capitalist society.

text: 不过，在这里还需要指出一点是，我不会诉诸某种道德考量或文化保守主义的立场，更为关键的地方在于，我并不知道共产主义对待性的态度将是怎样的，而在我看来，任何一种态度都是可取的：无论是保守或激进、无论是谴责出轨还是以出轨为荣抑或是根本没有轨，就其自身而言都是等值的——你没有办法指出这些态度和资产阶级法权有什么关系，更何况那个阶段也已经彻底消灭了资本主义法权及其所象征的普遍之维。
en: Yet, one further point must be noted: I shall not appeal to any moral consideration or cultural-conservative stance; what is more crucial is that I do not know what attitude communism will take towards sex, and it seems to me that any attitude is acceptable — whether conservative or radical, whether condemning adultery or taking pride in it or having no "track" at all — each is equal in itself. You cannot point to any relation between these attitudes and bourgeois right; still less, since that stage has already utterly abolished capitalist right and the universal dimension it symbolises.

text: 于是这些就都不过是差异与自由的呈现。
en: Thus these are all merely the manifestation of difference and freedom.

text: 关于这一点，战争是一个恰当的例子。
en: On this point, war is an apt example.

text: 当消除了阶级对立、民族纷争与地缘冲突以后，即铲除了战争的一切根由后，战争也就变成别无理由的了。
en: Once class antagonism, ethnic strife and geopolitical conflict are eliminated — that is, once all the roots of war are extirpated — war becomes something with no other reason.

text: 也就是说，我们没有任何理由来开始一场战争，于是我们可以仅仅为着战争自身而选择战争。
en: That is to say, we have no reason whatsoever to start a war, and so we may choose war solely for war's own sake.

text: 只有共产主义才能拥有如此崇高而纯粹的战争，不夹杂任何其他目的，甚至也没有敌人。
en: Only communism can possess so sublime and pure a war, with no other purpose mixed in, and not even an enemy.

text: 而在此所有行为都将是极度纯粹化的，并因而都可以成为目的本身。
en: And here all actions will be utterly purified, and may thereby become ends in themselves.

text: 在我看来共产主义将是癫狂的、扭曲的、极致化的、不可计数的、张力化的，或者它是和谐的、团结的、积极进取的、友爱互助的，为意义所充盈的，或者怎样都好。
en: In my view, communism will be frenzied, distorted, extreme, innumerable, tension-charged — or it will be harmonious, united, enterprising, mutually supportive and friendly, suffused with meaning — or anything at all.

text: 它唯独不可能是适度的，因为它永远在过程之中，也不可能有一个度。
en: The one thing it cannot be is moderate, for it is forever in process, and can have no measure.

text: 相反，倘若非社会自由根本不必然属于资本家，那么劳动者也不需要像形形色色的救赎宗教那样从屈服和苦难中寻找联合的理由。
en: Conversely, if non-social freedom does not fundamentally and necessarily belong to the capitalist, then workers need not, like the various redemptive religions, seek their reason for solidarity in submission and suffering.

text: 当自由人联合体由诸多“无族、无法、无家”的“孤子”所组成时，它不可能是那种以“我们”为重心的共同体，而是把他者性以一种全新的方式容纳在了集体之内或集体的成员之间。
en: When the association of free individuals is composed of many "stateless, lawless, homeless" "solitary sons," it cannot be the kind of community centred on "us"; rather, it accommodates otherness within the collective, or among the members of the collective, in a wholly new way.

text: 由于社会性不再被当作某种广袤而坚实的根基，劳动者在彼此的关联中就无法有效地援引任何超然的共识、律法、最大公约数等等，或者说他们除了一个个彼此以外别无所有（如果不考虑自然界的话）。
en: Since the social is no longer treated as some vast and solid foundation, workers, in their relations with one another, cannot effectively invoke any transcendent consensus, law, or common denominator, etc.; or rather, they have nothing but one another (if we set nature aside).

text: 这意味着他们各自的独特性和可变性不再被某种庞然大物反衬为不值一提的东西，而是完全以自身的面貌走上了前台。
en: This means that their respective uniqueness and mutability are no longer thrown into relief as trivial nothings by some leviathan, but step fully onto the stage in their own countenance.

text: 阿甘本〈Giorgio Agamben〉在这个意义上指出：
en: Agamben 〈Giorgio Agamben〉, in this sense, points out:

text: 正如正确的人类语词既不是对共同东西（即语言）的占用，又不是关于得体东西的交流，同样，人的面貌既不是通用面孔的个别化，又不是奇异特征的普遍化：它是随便什么〈whatever〉面貌，其中属于共同性质的东西和得体的东西是绝对无所谓的。
en: Just as the correct human word is neither an appropriation of the common (that is, language) nor a communication about what is proper, so too the human face is neither the individualisation of a generic face nor the universalisation of singular features: it is a whatever 〈whatever〉 face, in which what belongs to the common and what is proper is absolutely indifferent.

text: 这里的“随便什么”与日常含义恰好相反，指的不是无关紧要的东西，而是仅仅凭借它自身的各种属性而变得紧要的东西。
en: Here "whatever" is the exact opposite of its everyday meaning: it does not refer to something insignificant, but to something that becomes significant precisely by virtue of its own various attributes.

text: 因此，每一个“随便什么”都在其他“随便什么”面前显示出了最低限度的他者性。
en: Thus every "whatever" displays a minimal otherness before every other "whatever".

text: 进一步讲，正因为这种他者性是由个体，所以并没有任何属性被提升到特别的地位；相反，当今流行于发达国家的多元文化主义对性、宗教、民族等少数属性的强调是一种看似进步、其实在原则上相当平庸的做法。
en: Further, precisely because this otherness proceeds from the individual, no attribute is elevated to a special status; on the contrary, the multiculturalism prevalent in developed countries, with its emphasis on minority attributes such as sex, religion and ethnicity, is a practice that appears progressive yet is in principle rather banal.

text: 因此，由普遍化的非社会自由所带来的对他者性的肯定既有别于基于共同体的社会主义，又有别于自由主义的所谓左派或进步派。
en: Thus the affirmation of otherness brought about by universalised non-social freedom differs both from a community-based socialism and from the so-called left or progressive camp of liberalism.

text: 有时我当然会讥笑小市民，倒不是因为他们自甘保守，而是因为正是在他们自以为激进的时候才显示出如此保守。
en: Of course I do sometimes mock the petty bourgeois, not because they content themselves with conservatism, but because it is precisely when they imagine themselves radical that they reveal such conservatism.

text: 毕竟，他们的激进所有主张都可以概括为这一句话:
en: After all, every one of their radical claims can be summed up in this one sentence:

text: av自由，但是必须付钱！
en: av freedom, but one must pay!
